11	 *  adding the canonical name + an entry per source raw name below. */

13	  | "Read"
14	  | "Write"
15	  | "Edit"

89	  return ALIASES[rawName] ?? "Unknown";
90	}

104	 *  Mirrors OpenCovibe's getToolDetail() ordering. */
105	export function getToolDetail(input: unknown, rawToolName?: string): string {
106	  if (!input || typeof input !== "object") {
107	    return extractMcpAction(rawToolName) ?? "";
108	  }
109	  const o = input as Record<string, unknown>;
110	  const keys = [
111	    "file_path",
112	    "notebook_path",
113	    "path",
114	    "command",
115	    "cmd",
116	    "pattern",
117	    "query",
118	    "url",

121	    "subagent_type",
122	    "subagentType",
123	    "team_name",
124	    "subject",
125	    "skill",
126	    "recipient",
127	  ] as const;
128	  for (const k of keys) {
129	    const v = o[k];
130	    if (typeof v === "string" && v.trim()) return v;
131	  }
132	  // Fallback: extract action from MCP tool name pattern
133	  return extractMcpAction(rawToolName) ?? "";
134	}
135	
136	/** Extract short action name from MCP tool names like
137	 *  `mcp__plugin_{plugin}_{server}__{action}` → `{action}`. */
138	function extractMcpAction(rawName: string | undefined): string | undefined {
139	  if (!rawName || !rawName.startsWith("mcp__")) return undefined;
140	  const doubleUnderIdx = rawName.indexOf("__", 5); // skip first "mcp__"
141	  if (doubleUnderIdx === -1) return undefined;
142	  const action = rawName.slice(doubleUnderIdx + 2);
143	  return action || undefined;
144	}

Here is a summary of each file in `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/`:

---

**1. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/api.ts`**

The API client layer that talks to the Rust backend. It defines:

- TypeScript interfaces for every response shape the Rust server returns: `RustSessionSummary`, `RustMessage`, `RustSkillSummary`, `RustMcpSummary`, `RustSearchHit`, `RustStatsResponse`, `RustUsageOverview`, `RustFavoriteItem`, `RustHookEntry`, `RustAgentEntry`, `RustPluginEntry`, `RustCommandEntry`, `LogEntry`, `ImageMeta`, `SubagentMeta`, and more.
- A `request<T>()` helper that wraps `fetch()`, adds request IDs and session IDs as headers, logs latency, and deduplicates identical in-flight GET requests (to survive React StrictMode double-mounting in dev).
- A `rustApi` object (aliased as `api`) that exposes every REST endpoint: health/stats, skills, MCPs, session CRUD (list, detail, search, subagent, export, resume, refresh, trash/restore/permanent-delete), full-text search via POST, usage analytics, favorites, extensions (hooks/agents/plugins/commands), sources, logs, and an `openFolder` utility.
- Backward-compatible type aliases (e.g., `Message = RustMessage`, `SessionSummary = RustSessionSummary`) so existing component imports keep working.

---

**2. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/tool-rendering.ts`**

Render-time helpers for tool-call cards. It provides:

- `LANG_BY_EXT` -- a map from file extensions to syntax-highlighter language names (ts, py, go, rs, json, md, sql, etc.).
- `getLanguageFromPath(path)` -- extracts the language string from a file path by matching its extension.
- `isImagePath(path)` -- checks whether a path points to an image file (png, jpg, svg, gif, webp, etc.).
- `extractOutputText(output)` -- best-effort normalization of any tool output (string, array of content blocks, nested object with `text`/`content` fields, or plain JSON) into a single displayable string.
- `shortenPath(p)` -- truncates a long absolute path to its last two segments prefixed with an ellipsis.

---

**3. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/tool-colors.ts`**

Defines a per-tool color palette for the UI. Each `ToolColor` has Tailwind classes for `bg`, `text`, `border`, and an emoji `icon`. The `PALETTE` record maps both canonical names (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, etc.) and raw agent names (Shell, exec_command, read_file, list_dir, etc.) to their colors. Categories include:

- Blue for file reads, amber for writes/edits, emerald for shell/bash, purple for search/grep, fuchsia for directory listing, sky for web tools, cyan for agent/task, indigo for todo/plan, yellow for questions, rose for skills, red for delete, slate for wait/monitor, and sky for MCP calls.

`getToolColor(name)` looks up a tool name in the palette, falling back to `defaultToolColor`.

**4. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/tool-aliases.ts`**

Cross-agent tool name normalization. Different CLI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) use different names for the same conceptual tool. This file:

- Defines `CanonicalTool` as a union type of known canonical names: Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, Bash, Grep, Glob, LS, WebFetch, WebSearch, Task, TodoWrite, TodoRead, NotebookEdit, ExitPlanMode, AskUserQuestion, Skill, Permission, Unknown.
- Maintains an `ALIASES` record mapping raw agent tool names to canonical names (e.g., `Shell` -> `Bash`, `read_file` -> `Read`, `exec_command` -> `Bash`, `apply_patch` -> `Edit`, `codebase_search` -> `Grep`).
- `canonicalTool(rawName)` -- maps any raw tool name to its canonical equivalent.
- `isFileTool(name)` -- returns true for tools that read or write files (Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit).
- `getToolDetail(input, rawToolName)` -- extracts a short label from a tool's input object by scanning for common keys (file_path, command, pattern, query, url, description, etc.), with an MCP action-name fallback that strips the `mcp__...__` prefix.

**5. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/tool-result-pairing.ts`**

Pairs `tool_use` messages with their corresponding `tool_result` messages. Given a flat message list:

- Builds a map from `toolUseId` to the best matching `tool_result` message (preferring non-error results, otherwise taking the last one).
- Identifies all `tool_result` message IDs that are paired with a `tool_use` so they can be hidden from the primary message list (rendered inline within the tool-use card instead).

Returns `{ resultByToolUseId, hiddenIds }`.

**6. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/turn-grouping.ts`**

Groups a session's flat message list into conversational "turns". Each turn starts with a user message and includes all subsequent assistant/tool messages until the next user message.

- `buildTurns(messages)` returns an array of `TurnEntry` objects, each containing: the user message, a preview string (first line, max 60 chars, with XML wrapper cleanup), message count, tool count, error flag, and subagent count.
- `turnIndexForMessage(turns, msgIndex)` finds which turn a given message index belongs to, using a linear scan.
- Leading system/assistant messages before the first user message get bucketed into a synthetic turn 0 labeled "(系统消息)".

**7. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/hooks.ts`**

Custom React hooks:

- `useAsync<T>(fn, deps)` -- generic async data fetcher with `data`, `loading`, `error`, and `refetch` states. Supports cancellation on unmount.
- `useCachedAsync<T>(key, fn, deps)` -- SWR-style cached fetcher backed by a module-level `Map`. Returns cached data immediately on remount while revalidating in the background. The `loading` spinner only appears on the first fetch for a key; subsequent revalidations keep showing stale data.
- `invalidateAsyncCache(arg?)` -- clears the cache by exact key, by prefix, or entirely.
- `useDebounced<T>(value, delay)` -- standard debounce hook (default 200ms).

**8. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/xml-tag-parser.ts`**

Parses XML-like structured tags found in assistant messages (e.g., `<task-notification>`, `<system-reminder>`, `<teammate-message>`). It provides:

- `detectXmlTag(text)` -- checks if text starts with a recognized XML tag (must be registered in the tag registry).
- `parseXmlTag(text)` -- full parser that extracts the tag name, attributes, and nested content sections from one or more blocks of the same tag type. Returns `{ tagName, attrs, sections, blocks, raw }`.
- Internally, `parseSingleBlock` splits the inner content into `XmlSection` objects, where each section is either a named sub-tag or bare text (`__text__`).

**9. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/xml-tag-registry.ts`**

The registry of recognized XML tag configurations. Each `XmlTagConfig` defines: a display name (static or function of attributes), a Lucide icon, a color, and lists of field names categorized as meta, markdown, stats, or attribute fields. Currently registered tags:

- `task-notification` -- display name "任务通知", Bell icon, blue color, with meta fields (task-id, status, tool-use-id) and markdown fields (summary, result).
- `system-reminder` -- display name "系统提醒", Info icon, amber color.
- `teammate-message` -- dynamic display name based on `teammate_id` attribute, Users icon, dynamic color from attributes.

`resolveDisplay(cfg, attrs)` resolves the display name and color, handling both static and function-based values.

**10. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/highlight.tsx`**

Search-result highlighting utilities with both React and DOM approaches:

- `HighlightText({ text, q })` -- a React component that splits text into segments (via `highlightSegments` from a shared module) and wraps matches in `<mark class="search-mark">` elements.
- `highlightJsx(text, q)` -- function-call wrapper around `HighlightText`.
- `highlightDom(container, q)` -- DOM-level text walker that finds all TEXT_NODE descendants of a container, wraps case-insensitive matches in `<mark>` elements using Range/SurroundContents, and returns a cleanup function that restores the original DOM. Returns the total match count.
- `centerMarkInScroller(mark)` -- scrolls the nearest scrollable ancestor so that a given `<mark>` element is vertically centered, without triggering whole-page scroll.

**11. `/test/home/workspace/agent-panel/web/src/lib/ansi.ts`**

ANSI escape code handling for terminal output display. Uses the `ansi-to-html` library:

- `ansiToHtml(s)` -- converts ANSI color/style escape codes in a string to HTML markup.
- `hasAnsiCodes(s)` -- tests whether a string contains any ANSI escape sequences.
- `stripAnsi(s)` -- removes all ANSI escape codes from a string using regex replacement.
